balance_geometry.frame: base body frame, every joint at zero (the frame the support box is defined in); the superseded reading was world x at the settled pose

decision_rule.text: material = |mean delta vs nominal| > max(3.0 pts, 2x the nominal seed spread of that metric and horizon); resolved = the corner's seeds separate from nominal's by more than that same bar; an axis is reported as moved only when it is both, and every verdict carries the corner's own seed spread

superseded_rule.text: material = |delta| > max(3.0 pts, 2x the WORST nominal seed spread across all metrics)

decision_rule.pairing: seeds shared = same initial condition, NOT common random numbers; collect() draws sim.rng every tick for the push test, mode-dependently in Excitation and once per episode in fresh(), so two corners diverge at the first tick their dynamics differ and never realign
limits: forward-model prediction accuracy, not policy transfer
twin prediction across units; every real-log number is one unit, one phone

rows.corner: base -75 g at a fixed CoM
base +75 g at a fixed CoM

partition.oracle: MLP(128) trained on the corner's own first half (14741 windows, 20 epochs); frozen and oracle both scored on the held-out second half. It is a small-data model, so it is a LOWER BOUND on recoverable mismatch, NOT a ceiling: on the nominal body it scores BELOW the frozen model on every axis, and the size of that deficit is published per axis as oracle_deficit_on_nominal_body_pts
partition.fallen_definition: GrowBotSim.fallen(): |roll| > 1.2 or |pitch| > 1.2 rad; fall_rate is the FRACTION OF TICKS in that state, not the frequency of fall events
partition.seeds: every quantity carries its three seeds and their spread; thresholds are max(3.0 pts, 2x the nominal spread of that same quantity) and 'resolved' is the same unpaired seed-separation criterion the axis verdicts use
partition.denominators: frozen_drop/intrinsic/model_mismatch are HELD-OUT-half quantities; the axis table's delta_pts is the full-stream figure. They are different quantities and must not share a denominator
